CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to assess the efficacy of recent medication adjustments regarding anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, along with Mr. Smith's overall mental and physical health status.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed but slightly improved response to the recent changes in his treatment regimen. He states that since reducing trazodone to 50 mg at bedtime, his morning grogginess has lessened, allowing him to feel more alert during the day. However, he continues to experience nighttime awakenings, primarily around 2 AM, which disrupt his sleep quality. He reports sleeping approximately 6.5 to 7 hours per night, with some difficulty returning to sleep after these awakenings.
The patient indicates a marginal improvement in his fatigue levels, attributing this to a more consistent engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices, despite ongoing work-related stressors. He notes that his headaches have stabilized, occurring approximately 2-3 times per week, with a moderate intensity rated between 3-5 out of 10. Mr. Smith continues to manage his headaches with ibuprofen 400 mg as needed, which he reports is effective with no gastrointestinal side effects.
Mr. Smith expresses that he has made an effort to attend CBT sessions regularly, which he finds beneficial, although he still struggles to fully integrate mindfulness techniques into his daily routine. He has resumed acupuncture treatments bi-weekly, which he feels contributes positively to his overall well-being.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (adjusted) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (stable usage) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (increased) 7. Topiramate 50 mg daily 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, reporting that while project demands remain high, he is making a concerted effort to balance work with personal health activities. He is actively participating in his running group, which he finds beneficial for stress relief. He maintains a healthy diet, abstains from alcohol, and continues to limit caffeine intake to improve sleep quality.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep quality shows slight improvement; anxiety is manageable; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has stabilized; intensity is moderate; no visual disturbances or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Improved fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/74 mmHg, HR 72 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, appears more rested compared to previous visit. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Lorazepam remains at 1 mg as needed. Reiterate the importance of regular CBT attendance and mindfulness practice to further enhance anxiety management. 2. Insomnia: Continue trazodone at 50 mg at bedtime and melatonin at 10 mg. Monitor sleep quality closely for any further deterioration. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Maintain amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly and topiramate at 50 mg daily, with a follow-up in one month to reassess headache frequency and intensity. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to continue prioritizing physical activity and mindfulness practices. If fatigue does not show further improvement, consider a referral to a sleep specialist.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2029-05-01 to monitor symptoms, evaluate treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to reach out to the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
